stops.note: cognate with Latin 'dēns, dentis', as in 'dentist', perhaps meaning 'the eating one'
the 'n' dropped out, as in 'goose'; the plural 'tēþ' gave 'teeth'
'long in the tooth', old, refers to horses' gums receding with age

current_meaning: one of the hard white structures in the mouth used for biting
